deliverable: Built (not yet production-wired -- no consuming pipeline exists yet) the same-symbol overlapping-horizon embargo control that was N5's third, still-unbuilt blocker: leakage.py::embargo_overlapping_events(events, calendar, window=60) groups ResearchEvents by symbol, greedily keeps the earliest event in each same-symbol cluster, embargoes every later event within the window of an already-kept one, and resets the window on each fresh keep (so a +0/+61/+122-session run stays fully independent rather than being wrongly merged into one cluster by a naive distance-from-first check). Did NOT add a net-bps regression test -- the v4-regen handoff already flagged that gap; addressing it requires threading adv_series into the freeze_scan snapshot and is its own wave.
notes_limitations: Two real bugs closed in the export: (1) ResearchEvent has no .session attribute; session is recovered via event_store.session_of (event_id last ':' segment or timestamp.date()); (2) the first export included the negative-class archive (every scanned symbol-day) which the UI would mis-render as 'unknown' calls -- now filters to events where at least one detector returned VALID, matching the freeze_scan design intent. The v4-net-cost stamp is real but net_bps coverage is 0/11,591 (and 0/863,771 across the full archive): candidates.py::attach_outcomes looks up adv_value in the snapshot dict, which doesn't carry it. The fix (thread adv_series from build_future_map into freeze_scan snapshot) is its own wave -- this slice chose to make the gap visible in the UI rather than silently fill in fictional numbers. The export's wall-clock is ~5min for the load_events walk over 396 partitions; acceptable for nightly use, not for repeat reads. Risk: outcomes_2026-08-28.json is a single-date snapshot; the multi-date picker (UI plan row 5) is the next wave and will need a different JSON shape or a runtime fetch path.
